pr.title: Account for things that optimize out in inlining costs
pr.description:
This updates the MIR inlining `CostChecker` to have both bonuses and penalties, rather than just penalties.

That lets us add bonuses for some things where we want to encourage inlining without risking wrapping into a gigantic cost.  For example, `switchInt(const …)` we give an inlining bonus because codegen will actually eliminate the branch (and associated dead blocks) once it's monomorphized, so measuring both sides of the branch gives an unrealistically-high cost to it.  Similarly, an `unreachable` terminator gets a small bonus, because whatever branch leads there doesn't actually exist post-codegen.

The PR modifies CostChecker, which is exclusively consumed by the MIR inliner to decide whether a callee is cheap enough to inline. It changes cost() to use bonuses and adds bonuses/penalties for switch const/unreachable/etc. In inline.rs, the Inline pass constructs CostChecker and gates inlining on checker.cost() <= threshold. Thus this is pass-specific behavior knowledge for Inline. Library/test changes are supporting.

processing.reason: PR #126578 is not a semantic rewrite. It changes only the MIR inliner's profitability accounting: the old `CostChecker` accumulates penalties, while the new one returns `saturating_sub(penalty, bonus)` and rewards constructs expected to optimize away. The only consequence is whether a call is inlined, not the computed values of a well-defined program. The supporting library edit (`unchecked_sub` method → intrinsic) only avoids emitting a UbCheck and preserves behavior under the intrinsic's validity precondition; a differing execution would rely on UB, which Miri rejects. Encoding the two cost functions and showing different numeric costs would merely test the heuristic itself, not a source-level miscompile, and forcing a runtime value difference would require inventing an unrelated semantic rewrite. Therefore no source-grounded original-vs-transformed program pair can be validated as a semantic counterexample.

analysis.summary: MIR inlining profitability must account for MIR constructs that disappear before codegen. The historical PR changes Inline's CostChecker from a penalties-only accumulator to `penalty` minus `bonus`, rewarding constant `switchInt`, `Unreachable`, no-cost `Goto`/`Return`/non-dropping drops, disabled overflow checks, and disabled UB checks, while adding a penalty for large non-constant switches. This is an inlining-decision optimization, not a semantic bug fix.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the PR, `CostChecker` held one `cost: usize` and `cost()` returned `self.cost`. It ignored `StorageLive`, `StorageDead`, `Deinit`, and `Nop` statements, but added `INSTR_COST` for every other statement. For terminators it added `CALL_PENALTY` for a `Drop` whose type `needs_drop`, otherwise `INSTR_COST`; `CALL_PENALTY` for calls except direct intrinsic calls (`INSTR_COST`); `CALL_PENALTY` for every `Assert`; `RESUME_PENALTY` for `UnwindResume`; `INSTR_COST` for inline asm; and a catch-all `INSTR_COST` for all other terminators, including constant `SwitchInt`, `Unreachable`, `Goto`, and `Return`. There were no bonuses, so code expected to be eliminated still contributed positive cost.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the inliner estimated cost by accumulating only nonnegative instruction/call penalties, charging ordinary `+INSTR_COST` for constructs that codegen or later MIR cleanup removes: `SwitchInt` with a constant discriminant, `Unreachable`, `Goto`/`Return`, drops of types that do not need dropping, and `NullaryOp` constants. It also charged full `CALL_PENALTY` for optional overflow `Assert`s even when overflow checks were disabled, and had no offsetting bonus for `NullaryOp::UbChecks` when UB checks were disabled. Consequently the computed cost could exceed the inlining threshold even though the relevant branches/blocks/checks would not survive to codegen. The corrected model separates `penalty` and `bonus` and returns `usize::saturating_sub(self.penalty, self.bonus)`, adding `CONST_SWITCH_BONUS` for constant switches, `INSTR_COST` bonus for `Unreachable`, zero cost for `Goto`/`Return`, and reduced/offset costs for disabled overflow and UB checks.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies of candidate callees evaluated by the `Inline` pass, especially bodies near the inlining cost threshold that contain a `SwitchInt` whose discriminant is constant, `Unreachable`, trivial `Goto`/`Return`, non-dropping `Drop`, intrinsic statements, `Assert` terms marked as optional overflow checks, or `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::UbChecks, ..)`, under session settings such as `overflow_checks()` and `ub_checks()` being enabled or disabled. Include large non-constant `SwitchInt` with more than three targets as the opposing case. A paired test can use the same caller and callee MIR/source and apply only the old penalties-only cost transformation versus the new penalty-minus-bonus transformation.
analysis.trigger: The two cost models produce different decisions when an inline candidate's penalty-only cost is above the Inline threshold but its penalty-minus-bonus cost is at or below it, due to constant switches, unreachable arms/blocks, trivial control flow, non-dropping drops, disabled overflow checks, or disabled UB checks. Conversely, a candidate with a large non-constant switch may newly be penalized by `LARGE_SWITCH_PENALTY` and not inlined. Existing expected MIR changes show the new model inlining formerly non-inlined callees, e.g. `scope 1 (inlined <u16 as Step>::forward)` and `scope 4 (inlined <Map<impl Iterator<Item = T>, impl Fn(T) -> U> as Iterator>::next)`.
preconditions: The MIR `Inline` pass is evaluating a callee against its cost threshold.
The callee body contains MIR constructs that later optimization/codegen removes or simplifies, such as `SwitchInt` with `discr.constant().is_some()`, or `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`.
For disabled-check bonuses/reductions, the session must have `!tcx.sess.overflow_checks()` or `!tcx.sess.ub_checks()` as appropriate.
For the large-switch penalty, the switch discriminant must be non-constant and `targets.all_targets().len() > 3`.
A test must compare inlining output, not runtime behavior: this changes whether a call is inlined, not program semantics.
pitfalls: Do not classify this as a confirmed miscompile or a runtime bug fix; the PR changes an inlining profitability heuristic.
The bonus is not a negative cost: `cost()` is `usize::saturating_sub(self.penalty, self.bonus)`, so excess bonus clamps to zero rather than underflowing.

Constant `SwitchInt` receives a bonus only when `discr.constant().is_some()`; ordinary multi-target switches instead get `INSTR_COST`, and non-constant switches with more than three targets get `LARGE_SWITCH_PENALTY`.
`Unreachable` gets an `INSTR_COST` bonus, while `Goto` and `Return` are free and `UnwindTerminate` also has no added cost; do not keep the old catch-all `INSTR_COST` for these.
`NullaryOp` rvalues are generally free in the new model, but `NullaryOp::UbChecks` gets a `CALL_PENALTY` bonus only when UB checks are disabled.
An optional overflow `Assert` with `overflow_checks()` disabled is reduced from `CALL_PENALTY` to `INSTR_COST`, not made entirely free.
Intrinsic calls in terminators avoid `CALL_PENALTY`, but `NonDivergingIntrinsic::CopyNonOverlapping` as a statement gets `CALL_PENALTY` and `Assume` gets `INSTR_COST`.
`FalseUnwind`, `FalseEdge`, `Yield`, and `CoroutineDrop` are treated as `bug!("{kind:?} should not be in runtime MIR")`; tests should use runtime MIR, not pre-runtime constructs.

The library change from `len.unchecked_sub(offset)` to `crate::intrinsics::unchecked_sub(*len, offset)` removes an emitted UbCheck and can alter inlining/codegen expectations; do not attribute that directly to a changed Inline algorithm without checking the MIR.

`tests/crashes/123893.rs` adds an `#[inline(never)] fn more_cost()` call, showing unrelated regression tests may need extra cost to preserve the old inlining decision; do not "fix" expected inlining changes by forcing all old decisions back.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen` MIR tests that print MIR after `PreCodegen` inlining. Build paired caller/callee cases that differ only in the cost-model transformation: one with the historical penalties-only accounting and one with the PR's penalty-minus-bonus accounting. For positive-bonus constructs, put a constant-discriminant `switchInt`, unreachable arm, trivial `Goto`/`Return`, non-dropping drop, disabled optional overflow `Assert`, or disabled UB-check nullary op in the callee and choose sizes so old cost is just above the threshold while new cost is at/below it; assert that the new MIR contains `scope ... (inlined <callee>)` and has the call replaced by the callee body, while the old model leaves the call. For the opposite direction, use a non-constant `SwitchInt` with more than three targets so the new `LARGE_SWITCH_PENALTY` can suppress inlining. Exercise both `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind` where unwind actions affect `LANDINGPAD_PENALTY`, and set `overflow_checks`/`ub_checks` explicitly for the relevant cases. Existing tests provide concrete expected shapes: `checked_ops.step_forward` now inlines `<u16 as Step>::forward` through checked/wrapping arithmetic, and `loops.mapped` and `slice_iter.enumerated_loop` now inline iterator `next` chains. Also include a crash/regression case near the threshold to ensure changed costs do not produce invalid MIR. Do not claim execution or reproduction; these are test-construction guidelines only.
